title: Ephesus
kicker: Archaeology · Antiquity to the Middle Ages

blocks.tr: Efes, İzmir'in güneyinde, bugünkü Selçuk'un hemen yanında bir antik kenttir. İlk Çağ'ın en büyük ve en zengin kentlerinden biriydi. Bu topraklarda insanlar çok eskiden beri yaşıyor: kentin yakınındaki Çukuriçi Höyük'te sekiz bin yıldan eski bir köyün izleri var. Efes 2015'te UNESCO'nun dünya mirası listesine girdi.
blocks.en: Ephesus is an ancient city just outside today's Selçuk, south of Izmir. It was one of the largest and richest cities of the ancient world. People have lived here for a very long time: at Çukuriçi Höyük, a mound near the city, archaeologists have found the traces of a village more than eight thousand years old. In 2015 Ephesus was added to UNESCO's World Heritage List.

blocks.tr: Efes'i İyonyalı Yunanlar kurdu. Bir efsaneye göre kentin kurucusu Atinalı bir prens, Androklos'tu. Bir kâhinin sözüne göre yeni kentin yerini ona bir balık ve bir yaban domuzu gösterecekti. Bir gün adamları balık pişirirken bir balık tavadan sıçradı, ateş çalılara geçti ve çalıların arasından bir yaban domuzu kaçtı. Androklos domuzu avlayınca kentini oraya kurdu.
blocks.en: Ephesus was founded by Ionian Greeks. According to one legend, its founder was Androclus, a prince from Athens. An oracle had told him that a fish and a wild boar would show him where to build his city. One day, as his men were frying fish, a fish leapt out of the pan, the fire spread to the bushes, and a boar ran out of them. Androclus hunted the boar down and founded his city on that spot.

blocks.tr: Kentin en ünlü yapısı Artemis Tapınağı'ydı. Bu dev tapınak, dünyanın yedi harikasından biriydi. Tapınak MÖ 356'da yandı. Geleneğe göre ünlü olmak isteyen Herostratos adında bir adam onu bilerek yakmıştı. Plutarkhos'a göre Büyük İskender de aynı gece doğmuştu. Efesliler tapınağı yeniden yaptılar, ama MS 3. yüzyılda Gotlar onu da yaktı. Bugün tapınağın yerinde sadece temeller ve eski parçalardan oluşan tek bir sütun var.
blocks.en: The city's most famous building was the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders of the World. It burned down in 356 BCE. Tradition says that a man named Herostratus set fire to it on purpose because he wanted to be famous, and Plutarch adds that Alexander the Great was born that same night. The Ephesians rebuilt the temple, but in the 3rd century CE the Goths burned it too. All that stands on the site today are the foundations and a single column put together from old fragments.

blocks.tr: Büyük İskender öldükten sonra komutanlarından Lysimakhos, Efes'i yeni bir yere, bugün gezdiğimiz kalıntıların olduğu yere taşıdı. Romalılar zamanında Efes, Asya eyaletinin başkentiydi. Mermer caddelerinde tüccarlar, öğrenciler ve gezginler yürürdü. Zengin aileler tepedeki yamaç evlerde otururdu; bu evlerin duvar resimleri ve mozaikleri bugün de çok güzel.
blocks.en: After Alexander the Great died, one of his generals, Lysimachus, moved Ephesus to a new site, where the ruins we visit today stand. Under the Romans, Ephesus was the capital of the province of Asia. Merchants, students and travellers walked its marble streets, and rich families lived in the terrace houses on the hillside, whose wall paintings and mosaics are still beautiful today.

blocks.tr: Mermer caddenin sonunda Celsus Kütüphanesi duruyor. Celsus, Roma'nın Asya valisiydi. Kütüphaneyi 2. yüzyılın başında oğlu, babası için yaptı; Celsus'un mezarı kütüphanenin altında. Kütüphanede yaklaşık on iki bin kitap rulosu vardı. 262 yılında bir yangında binanın içi yandı, ön cephesi de yüzyıllar sonra bir depremde çöktü. Arkeologlar cepheyi 1970'lerde eski taşlarıyla yeniden kurdu.
blocks.en: At the end of the marble street stands the Library of Celsus. Celsus had been the Roman governor of Asia, and in the early 2nd century his son built the library in his honour; Celsus is buried beneath it. It held about twelve thousand scrolls. In 262 a fire gutted the building, and centuries later an earthquake brought down its façade. Archaeologists put the façade back up with its own stones in the 1970s.

blocks.tr: Kütüphanenin yakınındaki büyük tiyatroda on binlerce kişi oturabiliyordu. Ama Efes'in zenginliği limanından geliyordu ve Küçük Menderes Nehri'nin getirdiği toprak limanı yüzyıllar boyunca yavaş yavaş doldurdu. Kıyı giderek batıya kaydı. Liman dolunca gemiler Efes'e gelemedi ve insanlar kenti yavaş yavaş terk etti. Orta Çağ'da hayat yakındaki Ayasuluk tepesine taşındı; bugünkü Selçuk orada. Bugün eski liman, denizden birkaç kilometre uzakta.
blocks.en: Nearby, the great theatre could seat tens of thousands of people. But the wealth of Ephesus came from its harbour, and over the centuries the silt carried down by the Küçük Menderes river slowly filled it in. The shoreline moved further and further west. Once the harbour had silted up, ships could no longer reach Ephesus, and people gradually left the city. In the Middle Ages life moved to the nearby hill of Ayasuluk, where Selçuk stands today. The old harbour is now several kilometres from the sea.

blocks.tr: Avusturyalı arkeologlar Efes'te 1895'te kazıya başladılar. Kazılar başlayalı yüz yıldan fazla oldu ve arkeologlar bugün de çalışıyor.
blocks.en: Austrian archaeologists began excavating at Ephesus in 1895. More than a century has passed since then, and the work goes on today.

questions.q: According to the legend, what showed Androclus where to found his city?
options: A fish and a wild boar
questions.explain: *Yeni kentin yerini ona bir balık ve bir yaban domuzu gösterecekti*: the future in the past of [B1 unit 2](gp-future-in-past), **would show him**.

questions.q: Why did ships stop coming to Ephesus?
options: The river silted up the harbour
questions.explain: *Liman dolunca gemiler Efes'e gelemedi*: `-(y)IncA`, **once the harbour had filled up**.

questions.q: Who built the Library of Celsus?
questions.explain: *Kütüphaneyi … oğlu, babası için yaptı*: his son built it **for his father**.

sources.title: Ephesus
sources.note: Inscribed in 2015; settlement at Çukuriçi Höyük from the 7th millennium BCE; the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders, of which little remains; the Roman monuments; silting that moved the shoreline west; the medieval settlement on Ayasuluk Hill

sources.title: Ephesus
sources.note: A city of the Ionian League; the legend of Androclus, the fish and the boar; Lysimachus moved the city; capital of the province of Asia under Augustus; the theatre seated about 24,000 to 25,000; the harbour silted up by the Küçük Menderes, now about 5 km inland; Austrian excavations from 1895; the terrace houses

sources.title: Temple of Artemis
sources.note: One of the Seven Wonders; burned in 356 BCE, traditionally by Herostratus seeking fame; Plutarch links the fire to Alexander's birth; rebuilt, then destroyed in a Gothic raid in the 3rd century CE; today a single column assembled from fragments

sources.title: Library of Celsus
sources.note: Built from the 110s CE by Celsus's son in his honour; Celsus, proconsul of Asia, buried beneath it; about 12,000 scrolls; gutted by fire in 262; the façade fell in an earthquake and was re-erected in 1970–1978

sources.title: Ephesos: research history
sources.publisher: Austrian Archaeological Institute, Austrian Academy of Sciences
sources.note: Excavations began on 20 May 1895 under Otto Benndorf; the re-erection of the Library of Celsus completed in 1978; the terrace houses roofed in 1999–2000

sources.title: Ephesos
sources.note: The temple set on fire in 356 BCE by a man who wanted fame; the Library of Celsus (about 114–117 CE, over 12,000 scrolls) burned in the Gothic invasion of 262
